chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Courting and marrying Mamie Lawson of Spelman College
summary: Budd tells how Spelman was founded for fair-skinned children of white fathers, and how he persuaded his first wife to marry him in 1935.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: All of these -- well, the reason I know this story, cause her mother went to Spellman, also. And, --
Spellman College down in Georgia. And,
it was set up for these black kids who -- who were sired by rich white men by colored women. And, they -- mostly all of them were very fair. As you remember, my first wife.

And, well, she went to Spelman. So, I persuaded her after a year, let's get married. So, sure enough, in 1935, we got married. In the mean time, one day sitting at home I got this phone call from Ed Fox. Now --
